accent.displayName: Light-gold log link and chip edge

row.purpose: Single-line transcript previews, empty state and full-log action.

extensions.contrastException: White labels on solid gold retain the approved brand exception. This pairing does not establish ordinary small-text contrast compliance.
extensions.documentationEvidence: Refreshed against the implemented gold theme source and approved native gold previews. This is documentation of the approved palette and retained behavior, not accessibility certification.

nativeConventions.processingGlyph: Processing uses the surface token for its microphone glyph.
nativeConventions.previewPolicy: Native components are described without HTML/CSS substitutes.
nativeConventions.scope: Windows theme only; the headless macOS implementation is unchanged.

components.name: Recovery row
components.description: Native canvas row with a gold numbered chip, white numeral and light-gold edge. Neutral row hover; matching press and release or a physical digit copies the full transcript.

components.name: Full-log row
components.description: Light-gold link with a gold L chip. Click or physical L opens the full log.

components.name: Empty row
components.description: Muted noninteractive message with the transcript alignment.

components.name: Tray states
components.description: Gray idle and gold recording use a white microphone. Light-gold processing uses a charcoal microphone. Tooltips name the state.

narrative.overview: Dark neutral popup with gold shortcut chips, white labels and light-gold links. Native Windows recovery behavior is retained; the macOS port is headless and unchanged.
dos: Do retain the neutral palette, system type and restrained state colors.
Do keep every transcript and the full-log action reachable when the popup exceeds the work area.
Do preserve full transcript text behind shortened previews.
donts: Don't add decorative marketing imagery or an unrelated product flow.
Don't treat screenshots, keyboard shortcuts or system-DPI tests as full accessibility or mixed-DPI hardware certification.
